Ajahn, what is the main teaching you explore in this talk on 'this Dhamma reflection'?

In this talk, Ajahn Sumedho begins with the observation: *"Well, good afternoon, Luang Por. Good afternoon, Luang Por and John Trewick. Um so, today is April the 22nd and we're grateful that you're taking an opportunity to talk to us a bit today. And um having just come back from New Hampshire, uh people are asking and others are always asking how you're..."* The invitation throughout is to turn attention away from conceptual analysis and toward the direct quality of knowing itself — the luminous, non-verbal awareness that is present before thought arises. This is the heart of practice: not achieving a special state, but recognising the unconditioned peace already here as *sati* (mindfulness) itself. Rest in that natural openness.

Ajahn, what does it mean to rest in pure awareness rather than being lost in thought?

Ajahn Sumedho offers this pointer: *"As you mentioned the identification with

the body, uh what are ways that you explore identification with the mind in reference to pure consciousness and pure awareness?"* Pure awareness (Buddho — the knowing quality) is the silent background against which all thoughts, emotions, and perceptions appear and dissolve. It is not produced by effort; it is what we already are before mental commentary begins. The practice is simply to notice the noticing — the aware space itself — rather than chasing the objects appearing within it. In this very moment, rest in the knowing that is reading these words.

Rather than taking this as a concept to memorise, use it as a mirror: where do you notice saṃyojana showing up right now in your body, mood, or thought? The Dhamma is not a philosophy to be studied from outside but a living reality to be seen clearly from within the laboratory of awareness. Let this teaching dissolve into direct knowing.
